AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: The aim of this review is to document pain assessment tools used primarily for older adults in long-term care facilities and compare self-report and observer-rated tools.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A literature search was conducted in Ovid MEDLINE(®), Embase, Cochrane and PsycINFO. Keywords included 'dementia', 'pain management' and 'managing pain'.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Of 1033 references, 23 articles were selected for inclusion. Six tools were self-rated and 18 tools were administered by an observer. 13 studies evaluated the reliability/validity of their scales; four studies compared different scales against each other.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Self-report should be the first-line approach when possible, with observational assessment used as a supplementary tool. Reliable observational tools have been shortened, and shown to maintain high reliability/validity, and positive psychometric properties.
